note: Exceptions for scripts/check-glossary-terms.mjs. `include` is the doc set that carries Wynding's game vocabulary; ADRs and design-notes are deliberately out of scope — they are engineering prose, where these words (save, layer, field, digest) carry their ordinary technical senses and would cost far more exceptions than the drift they would catch. `ignoredTerms` are avoided words whose other sense cannot be told apart mechanically. `allowedSenses` are case-insensitive regexes over a line of prose: a hit inside a match is a different sense, not drift; keep them narrow, since a loose pattern exempts the next real violation on the same line. Every entry states why; an entry that matches nothing fails the check. See docs/ai-workflow.md.

ignoredTerms.why: The glossary itself allows it: "interchangeable in prose, but 'path' is canonical in code" — so linting it in docs would contradict the entry it comes from.
Unavoidable generic English in these docs — grid unit, fixed-point units, unit of work, unit-tested. Telling those from 'unit' meaning a tower needs grammar, not grep.
Every use here is the verb ("shapes the route by building", "Building is allowed while paused"). Only the noun is drift, and a grep cannot tell them apart.
Engine is itself a canonical term (the determinism toolkit), so flagging the word would tell an author to rename the thing it is named after. Only "engine" meaning the sim is drift.
A save is its own concept per the Replay entry's aside and ADR 0008 — a state snapshot. Only calling a replay a save is drift, and that reads identically to a grep.
The ordinary verb ("update the HUD", "an app update") is everywhere; only "update" meaning one tick is drift.

allowedSenses.why: "Core Gameplay" is PRD 0001's title and "core loop" is the game's central loop — neither names the engine package.
The deterministic/byte-identity/web core is the codebase's centre in the ordinary sense, not the Engine package being renamed.
Modelling prose — the damage/grid/domain model is a set of rules, not the sim package.
The genre name ("tower defense", "fixed-lane defense") and the player's defenses as a whole — not armor, the stat.
Names the whole damage system in PRD 0001 §5; the stat inside it is still called armor.
A tower's upgrade level, which is real vocabulary — not a board, wave, or difficulty tier.
The pathfinding algorithm (flow-field + A*), not the board.
A schema field — "the `boardId` field in ADR 0006" — the data-record sense.
A creep durability stat, per the Creep entry's own wording. Score is the thing that must not be called points.
Geometry: creeps are points on the fine grid.
The glossary's own note — HP is a creep stat; only the player's lives must not be called HP. Deliberately narrow: "the player's HP" has to keep failing.

A wave launches, auto-launches, or is launched by an early call — the wave-start sense, not a release. Deliberately requires the wave to be launching or be launched: "we launch after the last wave" is still drift.
The launch tick, and "launch + N ticks" — the tick a wave starts on.
The adjective — "high durability", "one high-impact discharge". Written as a negative, so the grading sense the P0–P3 entry rejects ("high severity", "high-priority") is not exempted and still fails.
Medium is a difficulty-tier name (Easy/Medium/Hard), not a severity label. Kept linted rather than ignored so "medium severity" still fails.
The Phase entry's own definition — "a coherent stage of the product" — defining the canonical term in plain English.
Something delivered in a phase or release line, not a milestone renamed.
The elemental damage-type system PRD 0001 rules out — not a creep's domain.
A tower or creep variant, the roadmap's and PRD's slice vocabulary — not a creep's ground-vs-air domain. Scoped to those two docs so a milestone spec cannot use it to call a domain a type.
Structural metaphor for the product taking shape, not a rendered frame.
A newly added layer of tuning, not a creep's domain.
The sim's scheduled-impact event queue, not a player command awaiting a tick.
The severity entry says there is no P4 — it has to name it to rule it out.
The Creep entry defines the canonical term in plain English.
